newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to sell Banco Latino by Dec 15.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to sell Banco Latino by Dec 15.

text.p: Venezuela plans to auction state-owned bank Banco Latino before December 15, the bank's president said Wednesday.

"December 15 is the date we have proposed to have the process resolved and completed of privatizing Banco Latino and the conglomerate of companies in the Latino financial group," Banco Latino President Rolando Salcedo told a news conference.
Salcedo said the aim was to auction the bank via the Caracas Stock Exchange in much the same way as the bank sold off 59 branches via the exchange earlier this year in a downsizing effort.
Asked to put a price on the group's worth, he said, "In an a priori estimate, the auction price could be about 37 billion bolivars ($78 million)."

The Banco Latino which will be sold this year will be very different from the bank that was once the second largest in Venezuela and whose collapse in January 1994 sparked a two-year crisis in the banking sector, Salcedo explained.
Under the bank sale plan, leasing company Arfinan, which belongs to the Latino group, will be converted into a commercial bank. Banco Latino as an entity would disappear.

"The new bank will become the head of the group...In this case, Banco Latino is not being sold. The bank's network of agencies is being sold including assets liabilities and personnel as was the case with the sale of branches in July," Salcedo said.

The auction will therefore include Banco Latino's remaining 49 branches, five drive-in banks, an automatic teller network with over 367,000 clients and the bank's holdings of government and central bank paper, he said.
"Banco Latino as such will disappear," he added.
What remains of the bank, which should be about 70 billion bolivars worth of assets including credit portfolios, will be run as a separate company until it can be liquidated, Salcedo said.
"This institution, which will not be dedicated to financial intermediation, will be a simple commercial business whose mission is to resolve every problem until its eventual liquidation," he said.
Salcedo explained that this company would absorb any legal suits against the bank, and group together those assets which are not attractive enough to be privatized.
Banco Latino was taken over by the government in January 1994 and subsequently re floated.
It was the country's eighth biggest bank in terms of deposits at the end of August with 134.779 billion bolivars ($284 million).
